newsitem.title: MALTA: Turnover soars on Malta stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Turnover soars on Malta stock exchange.

text.p: Malta stock exchange turnover in the once-weekly trading soared to Lm13.4 million ($34.8 million) on Wednesday from Lm5.3 million the previous week, following a high level of trading in government stocks.
There were 130 deals, of which 84 were in fixed income securities and 46 in equities. The value of the share index rose by a point to reach 987.84 points.
Trading in government stocks reached Lm13.3 million, reflecting significant participation of institutional investors.

Business in corporate bonds reached just under Lm20,000, of which Lm16,000 represented business in the 6.5 per cent Gasan bonds 1998/99, which were traded at an average price of 98.5, giving a current yield of 6.6 percent. There was Lm4,000 worth of business in Mid-Med Bank's unsecured loan stock 2005 at an average of 100.07. The current yield for this bond in 7.24 percent.
Trading in equities maintained the previous week's levels at Lm74,000.
The value of trading in Bank of Valletta amounted to almost Lm50,000 at an average price of 123 cents per share, unchanged from the previous week.
Trading in Mid-Med Bank reached Lm13,000, with the average share price dropping one cent to 153 cents.
A total of 7,500 Lombard Bank Malta shares were traded for an average 140 cents, unchanged, and 600 Middle Sea Insurance shares traded at 122 cents, up one cent.
There was no trading in Farsons ordinary shares, but three deals were struck in the company's 8.5 percent preference shares, the total value reaching less than Lm200. ($1: Lm0.37c)
